about: S5AA R51's CONTROL CORPUS, the successor to S5 2s.1's s5-control. The owner's decision of 2026-10-03 on AA1-25(c) turns spending flexibility off by default (defaultPlan.retirement.flexibility 10 -> 0), and every golden and targeted control scenario inherits the default, so sixteen control scenarios mean different plans. Control rule 3 makes that its own versioned corpus change, in its own commit (b722884, the default and nothing else), and rule 5 keeps the old capture beside the new one. The owner chose this successor control on 2026-10-03 (the S5 precedent), over freezing the control at the old default. The predecessor record is kept whole below. tests/control-corpus.test.js holds this record to the live corpus and to its evidence.
name: s5aa-r51-control

evidence.what: the control capture itself: taken at b722884, qualified, and reproduced byte for byte by that commit's own capture tool in a second clean worktree

controlCapture.takenIn: a clean worktree checked out at b722884 (node_modules a junction to the main checkout's, jsdom 30.0.1), Windows 11, Node 24.17.0; taken twice in two clean worktrees, byte-identical. b722884 is on the branch: its tree holds the new default with the old record, so its own control tests fail, as e157733's did (Q77, answer (a)); unlike e157733 it needs no tag to stay reachable.
controlCapture.why: the default change makes sixteen control scenarios different plans: the five golden scenarios (golden:baseline, golden:monte-carlo-fixed-seed, golden:rmd-and-roth-conversion, golden:reserve-and-bond-tent, golden:guardrails-withdrawal-strategy) and the eleven targeted ones, each inheriting the default flexibility. The twenty generated seeds draw their own flexibility and are unchanged. The corpus-input hash moves from 343387a9 to dbbe8036. Predicted before any capture by audit/S5AA/R51/S5AA_R51_PREDICTION_RECORD_20261003.md (d663f16); the capture replays exactly against b722884 (tools/historical-replay.js, ROUND-TRIP PASS).

replay.decided: Question 10 (A), the owner, 2026-09-16: control test 4.7 holds the stored control capture to the engine that captured it (historical integrity), and today's engine to a written prediction (candidate movement), as two separate checks. A passing replay approves no candidate output.
replay.reference: the capture's own meta, written when it was taken: gitCommit, the sha256 of every declared input (meta.inputGraph.files) and the Node version (meta.inputGraph.runtime.node). Every declared input is verified before anything runs.
replay.sources: in order: a reference tree the caller names (--reference-tree, or the CORPUS_REFERENCE_TREE environment variable); this repository's git objects (b722884 is a commit on sprint/s5aa-r51, kept by every merge of that branch); a reference-trees directory named by the full commit at the repository root, written by the tool's materialize command; this control's is committed, so a source package carries it. With none available the replay is BLOCKED, never a pass, and today's engine is never used in its place.
replay.qualifiedEnvironment: the capture's recorded Node version on Windows (Windows 11 with Node 24.17.0); anything else is UNQUALIFIED and nothing runs. Exact replay on a second machine or another Node version is not established, and no tolerance is applied.
replay.notReplayed: the 11 targeted scenarios, built only inside tools/capture-baseline.js: reported as not replayed by name, and still covered by INVENTORY, ENCODING, NON-VACUOUS and SHAPE.

rules: The control corpus does not change. A scenario may be ADDED under a new name; a name never comes to mean a different plan, and compareInputs() reports it as INCOMPATIBLE if one does.
A candidate engine is compared with the control capture on the control inputs. Added scenarios are evaluated by BOTH the reference and the candidate engine before anything about them is compared.
Any input or generator edit is its own versioned change, with its old and new input hashes and a reason, in its own commit (ground rule 7). It is never folded into an instrument or engine commit.
A diffSnapshots() refusal is never bypassed. compareInputs() explains a refusal; it does not lift one.
Old captures remain. Neither the control capture nor any stored baseline it cites is edited.
